results.title: What Is Agentic Video Editing? How It Works | Arsaze
results.content:
## Why the timeline matters

A finished video is hundreds of small decisions. If an AI hands back only a rendered file, every change means starting over. When the agent works on a real multi-track timeline, its decisions stay visible and editable: you can move one cut, swap one shot or change one caption, and so can the agent on its next pass.

That is why Arsaze is built as a complete editor first. Tracks, clips, trims, transitions, keyframes, color grading and audio mixing are all there for a person, and the same editor is open to AI assistants. People often call it Cursor for video editing.

## What an agent can do in Arsaze today [...] ArsazeArsaze

Agentic video editing

# Agentic video editing, explained

Agentic video editing is video editing done by an AI agent that works through a whole edit in steps: it looks at the footage, plans the cut, makes the edits on a real timeline, checks the result and fixes what is wrong, while a person can watch, step in or undo at any point. Arsaze is an agentic video editor: Claude, ChatGPT, Grok or the built-in Arsaze assistant edit the same multi-track timeline you do, and every edit plays back live and is saved to version history.

 Open a project, add your footage and describe the edit you want, the way you would brief a human editor.
 Watch it work, step in when you want, and export when you are happy.

## Questions and answers

### What is agentic video editing?

Agentic video editing is when an AI agent carries out a whole edit in steps toward a goal: it reviews the footage, plans the cut, edits a real timeline, checks the result and fixes what is wrong, while a person can watch, step in or undo. Arsaze is a video editor built for this, and Claude, ChatGPT and Grok can operate it.
